name: Antara ibn Shaddad
bio: The most famous horseman of pre-Islamic Arabia and a poet of the first rank, of the tribe of Abs in Najd. His mother was an Abyssinian slave named Zabiba, and by the custom of the time his father counted him a slave, until raiders struck the Abs and his father told him to charge; Antara answered that a slave knows only how to milk, and his father said, “Charge, and you are free,” as Ibn Qutayba tells it. He loved his cousin Abla, who appears in nearly all his poems, composed one of the Mu'allaqat, “Hal ghadara al-shu'ara'”, and fought in the war of Dahis and al-Ghabra'. He lived long and was killed about 22 years before the Hijra (around 600 CE), by al-Asad al-Rahis or by Jabbar ibn Amr of Tayyi'. Much verse was later put in his mouth, so that al-Zirikli says of his printed diwan that “most of it is fabricated”, and he became the hero of the folk epic Sirat Antar.
